questions.q: Which of the following electrical terms refers to the rate of flow of electric charge, measured in Amperes?
questions.n: Current is the actual flow of electrons through a conductor, quantified in Amperes (Amps).

questions.q: In a residential project, which safety device is specifically designed to protect people from electric shock in wet areas like bathrooms and kitchens?
questions.n: GFCIs monitor the balance of current and trip instantly if a leak to ground is detected, preventing electrocution.

questions.q: What is the unit of measure for the total amount of light emitted by a source in all directions?
questions.n: Lumen is the standard unit for luminous flux, indicating the total 'quantity' of light produced by a lamp.

questions.q: According to standard electrical practice, what is the maximum number of outlets allowed on a 20-ampere general-purpose branch circuit?
questions.n: Standard practice typically limits a 20-amp circuit to 10 outlets based on an assumed load of 180 volt-amperes per outlet.

questions.q: Which type of conduit is characterized by having thin walls and being easily bent by hand or with a small bender, commonly used in exposed indoor locations?
questions.n: EMT is a thin-walled steel raceway that is lightweight and easily manipulated for interior branch wiring.

questions.q: What is the standard frequency of alternating current (AC) electricity supplied in the Philippines?
questions.n: The Philippines follows the North American standard of 60 cycles per second (Hertz) for its power grid.

questions.q: In electrical wiring, the 'Gauge' of a wire refers to its thickness. Which of the following statements is true regarding wire gauge numbers (AWG)?
o: The larger the number, the thicker the wire.
The smaller the number, the thicker the wire.
The number indicates the maximum voltage the wire can carry.
The number refers to the length of the wire in meters.
questions.n: Lower AWG numbers (like #8) represent much thicker wires with higher current-carrying capacity than higher numbers (like #14).

questions.q: What architectural component is used to house the main circuit breakers and distribute power to different branch circuits within a building?
questions.n: Also known as the breaker box or distribution board, the panelboard accepts the main power feed and divides it into individual circuits.

questions.q: A 'Three-Way Switch' setup allows you to control a single light fixture from how many different locations?
questions.n: A three-way switch configuration uses two switches to control one light, common at the top and bottom of stairs.

questions.q: Which term describes the loss of voltage that occurs as electricity travels through a long run of wire due to the resistance of the conductor?
questions.n: Voltage drop is the decrease in electrical potential along the path of a current, which can cause equipment to malfunction if the wire is too long or too thin.

questions.q: Which specific type of electrical conduit is recommended for underground installations or areas highly exposed to corrosion, such as coastal residential projects?
questions.n: PVC is moisture-resistant and immune to corrosion, making it the standard choice for underground and coastal applications.

questions.q: When designing a reflected ceiling plan, you need to provide 'Task Lighting.' What is the primary purpose of this lighting layer?
o: To highlight architectural features or artwork.
To create a decorative pattern on the ceiling.
To provide high-intensity light for specific activities like reading or cooking.
To provide general illumination for the entire room.
questions.n: Task lighting focuses light on a specific area to assist the user in performing detailed visual work.

questions.q: What is the standard minimum mounting height for a wall-mounted convenience outlet (ACU outlets excluded) in a typical residential living room, measured from the finished floor line (FFL)?
questions.n: A height of 300mm (roughly 12 inches) is the standard architectural practice for general-purpose wall outlets.

questions.q: In the context of the Philippine Electrical Code (PEC), what does the 'Demand Factor' represent in electrical load calculations?
o: The speed at which a circuit breaker trips.
The maximum voltage a building can handle.
The ratio of the maximum demand to the total connected load.
The amount of electricity lost during transmission.
questions.n: The demand factor accounts for the fact that not all electrical loads in a building will be turned on at the same time.

questions.q: Which electrical component is used to convert high-voltage electricity from the utility company (e.g., 13.2 kV) to the lower voltage used within a building (e.g., 220V)?
questions.n: Transformers use electromagnetic induction to step down (or step up) voltage levels for distribution.

questions.q: In lighting design, the 'Coefficient of Utilization' (CU) is used to account for which of the following factors?
o: The cost of electricity per kilowatt-hour.
The efficiency of the fixture and the room's surface reflectances.
The heat generated by the lighting fixtures.
The age of the light bulb.
questions.n: The CU measures how effectively a specific luminaire delivers light to the work plane based on room proportions and surface colors.

questions.q: For safety and maintenance, what is the minimum required clear working space in front of an electrical panelboard or switchgear?
questions.n: A minimum clearance of 900mm (approx. 3 feet) is generally required to allow for safe access and movement.

questions.q: Which of the following describes a 'Short Circuit'?
o: A light switch that only works half the time.
A circuit that is too small for the room.
An accidental low-resistance connection between two conductors.
questions.n: A short circuit occurs when current bypasses the load and takes a path of least resistance, causing a massive surge of current.

questions.q: Emergency lighting and exit signs must be able to provide illumination for a minimum duration of how long after the main power fails?
questions.n: The standard requirement (including RA 9514) for emergency lighting is a minimum of 1.5 hours (90 minutes) of operation.

questions.q: A residential kitchen plan includes a 1.5 HP window-type air conditioning unit. According to standard practice, how should this appliance be circuited?
o: Connected to the nearest general-purpose convenience outlet circuit.
Provided with a dedicated individual branch circuit.
Shared with the kitchen lighting circuit to save on conduit.
Connected directly to the main service entrance without a breaker.
questions.n: Large motorized appliances require their own circuit to handle high starting currents and continuous operational loads safely.

questions.q: In the Philippines, what is the standard color used for the 'Grounding' wire in a typical electrical installation?
o: Green or Green with Yellow stripes
questions.n: Green is the internationally recognized color code for safety grounding wires, as specified in the PEC.

questions.q: When an architect is coordinating a large commercial project with a 'Transformer Vault,' which of the following is a critical code requirement for the vault's door?
o: It must be a 3-hour fire-rated door and must swing outward.
It must be a sliding door to save hallway space.
It must be made of solid wood for better insulation.
It must be painted bright yellow for high visibility.
questions.n: Vault doors must prevent fire spread and swing outward to allow for easy emergency egress during a blast or fire.

questions.q: The PEC defines the 'Service Drop' as which part of the electrical system?
o: The main grounding rod driven into the earth.
The wires connecting the panelboard to the outlets.
The overhead wires from the utility pole to the building's attachment point.
The underground pipes used for electrical wiring.
questions.n: The service drop is the specific overhead connection provided by the utility company (like Meralco) to the customer.

questions.q: Why is the 900 mm minimum clearance in front of a panelboard strictly enforced by inspectors?
o: To ensure an electrician can jump back safely and have room to work without obstruction.
To accommodate the size of the electrical meter.
To provide adequate ventilation for the breakers.
To allow space for a desk or workstation for the electrician.
questions.n: In the event of an arc flash or emergency, the worker needs unobstructed space to move and access components.

questions.q: Which of the following is a primary function of 'Bonding' in an electrical system?
o: To increase the voltage of the system.
To ensure electrical continuity and provide a safe path for fault current.
To insulate the wires from the conduit.
To reduce the monthly electricity bill.
questions.n: Bonding connects all metallic non-current-carrying parts to ensure they are at the same potential and provide a path to ground.

questions.q: In a commercial office building, what is the 'Demand Factor' typically applied to the general lighting load to determine the size of the service entrance?
questions.n: For offices and hospitals, the first 50,000 volt-amperes (VA) or more are often calculated at 100% demand because office lights stay on.

questions.q: Which type of lighting fixture distribution directs 90% to 100% of the light output downward toward the work surface?
questions.n: Direct lighting fixtures direct the vast majority of their light output straight down onto the task area.

questions.q: A 'UPS' (Uninterruptible Power Supply) is most essential for which type of architectural space?
questions.n: A UPS provides near-instantaneous power during a failure to prevent data loss and equipment damage before a generator kicks in.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a 'Busbar' within a large industrial switchgear?
o: To protect the system from lightning strikes.
To act as a high-capacity conductor that collects and distributes large amounts of current.
To measure the amount of energy consumed by the building.
To serve as a structural support for the cabinet.
questions.n: Busbars are solid metal bars (usually copper or aluminum) that can carry much higher currents than standard cables.

questions.n: For steep roofs (4 in 12 or greater), the PEC allows a reduced clearance of 1.0 meter (1000 mm) since the slope prevents people from easily walking on it.

questions.q: A 'Four-Way Switch' is used in conjunction with two 'Three-Way Switches' to control a light from how many locations?
questions.n: To control a light from three spots, you must place one four-way switch between two three-way switches.

questions.q: In electrical load calculations, a 'Continuous Load' is defined as a load where the maximum current is expected to continue for how long?
questions.n:
Loads expected to run for 3 hours or more (like store lighting) are continuous and require a

125% multiplier for circuit sizing.

questions.q: What architectural feature is required at the point where the service entrance conductors enter the building to prevent water from entering the conduit?
questions.n: The weatherhead or service cap is the waterproof entry point designed to let wires out while keeping rain out of the raceway.

questions.q: Which type of 'Box' is typically used for mounting heavy ceiling fans to ensure structural and electrical safety?
o: Octagonal Steel Box with Fan-Rated Brace
questions.n: Fan-rated boxes are reinforced to support the weight and movement of the fan without loosening or falling.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between a 'Step-down Transformer' and a 'Step-up Transformer'?
o: One uses AC and the other uses DC.
One increases voltage while the other decreases it.
One is installed underground and the other is overhead.
One is for lighting and the other is for power.
questions.n: Step-up transformers increase output voltage (for transmission), while step-down transformers decrease it (for building use).

questions.q: For architectural coordination, where should 'Smoke Detectors' ideally be placed in a residential bedroom?
o: Near the air conditioning supply vent.
In the corner of the wall and ceiling.
Directly above the headboard of the bed.
On the ceiling, at least 100 mm from the wall.
questions.n: Placing detectors away from corners ensures they are in the path of rising smoke flow.

questions.q: A 'Circuit Breaker' provides two types of protection. One is for 'Short Circuits.' What is the other?
questions.n: Overload protection handles situations where too many devices are plugged in, heating the circuit slowly over time.

questions.q: Which material is the most common conductor used in building wiring due to its excellent conductivity and flexibility?
questions.n: Copper is the gold standard for interior wiring because of its superior electrical conductivity and durability.

questions.q: When calculating the lighting load for a 'Residential' occupancy according to the PEC, what is the standard unit load value per square meter of floor area?
questions.n: The Philippine Electrical Code specifies 24 VA per square meter as the baseline for general lighting loads in residential dwellings.

questions.q: If a service drop conductor passes over a flat roof that is 'walkable' or used as a roof deck, what is the minimum required vertical clearance?
questions.n: For surfaces subject to pedestrian traffic, such as roof decks, a minimum clearance of 2.5 meters (2500 mm) is mandatory for safety.

questions.q: Which specific 'trip mechanism' in a standard circuit breaker is responsible for protecting the circuit against a slow, sustained 'Overload'?
questions.n: The thermal element bends as it heats up over time, providing protection against cumulative overloads from too many devices.

questions.q: In a large commercial kitchen, what type of conduit is required for wiring that is exposed to physical damage and high moisture from steam and cleaning?
questions.n: RMC provides the highest level of physical protection and is threaded for watertight connections in industrial environments.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between 'Lumens' and 'Lux'?
o: Lumens measure light at the source; Lux measures light falling on a surface.
Lux is the metric unit; Lumens is the English unit.
Lumens measure color temperature; Lux measures brightness.
There is no difference; they are interchangeable.
questions.n: Lumens (Luminous Flux) is the total light output, while Lux (Illuminance) is Lumens per square meter on a work plane.

questions.q: According to the PEC, what is the 'Maximum Demand' for the first 3000 VA of a residential general lighting load?
questions.n: The first 3000 VA of a residential lighting load is always calculated at 100% because it is the baseline usage.

questions.q: Which electrical device is used to change the path of current in a circuit, often found in 'Transfer Switches' for emergency generators?
questions.n: A double-throw switch allows a load to be connected to one of two different power sources (Utility or Generator).

questions.q: In a residential bathroom, a GFCI outlet must be installed if the outlet is within how many meters of a water source (like a lavatory or tub)?
o: All outlets in a bathroom must be GFCI protected, regardless of distance.
Only if it is within reach of the shower.
questions.n: The PEC requires all bathroom receptacles to have GFCI protection due to the high risk of shock in wet environments.

questions.q: What is the standard purpose of 'Lightning Arresters' installed at the service entrance of a building?
o: To divert high-voltage surges from lightning strikes safely to the ground.
To attract lightning to the building for power generation.
To stop the rain from entering the conduits.
To lower the electrical resistance of the building.
questions.n: Arresters protect the building's electrical system from massive voltage spikes caused by external lightning strikes.

questions.q: When coordinating with a Mechanical Engineer, an Architect must ensure the 'Generator Room' has enough of which architectural feature for the engine to function?
o: Adequate intake and exhaust louvers for ventilation.
Large glass windows for natural lighting.
questions.n: Generators require massive amounts of air for combustion and cooling to prevent overheating and engine failure.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a 'Fuse' in a building's electrical system?
o: To increase the voltage for heavy appliances.
To store electricity for use during a power outage.
To convert Alternating Current (AC) to Direct Current (DC).
To break the circuit by melting a metal strip when current exceeds a safe level.
questions.n: A fuse is a sacrificial device that protects the circuit from overcurrent by physically melting and opening the path.

questions.q: In a reflected ceiling plan, what does the symbol 'S3' typically represent?
o: A circuit with three light fixtures.
questions.n: In standard architectural drafting, the 'S' represents a switch and the subscript '3' indicates it is a three-way type.

questions.q: Which of these is the most common voltage supplied to a standard residential convenience outlet in the Philippines?
questions.n: The nominal voltage for residential power in the Philippines is 230V (often referred to as 220-240V range).

questions.q: When an architect provides a 'Service Entrance' for a small house, which component acts as the final 'link' between the utility wires and the house wiring?
questions.n: The meter is the interface point where utility power is measured before entering the building's main distribution panel.

questions.q: Why is 'Aluminum' wiring often discouraged for small-scale residential interior branch circuits compared to 'Copper'?
o: It has a tendency to expand and contract more, which can loosen connections.
It is more expensive than copper.
It is too flexible and breaks easily when bent.
It is much heavier than copper.
questions.n: Aluminum's thermal expansion properties can lead to loose connections and 'arcing' if not installed with specific rated connectors.

questions.q: What is the standard vertical clearance for a service drop conductor passing over a residential driveway?
questions.n: The PEC requires a minimum of 3.7 meters (3700 mm) over residential driveways to prevent contact with vehicles.

questions.q: In a basic lighting circuit, which wire is connected to the 'Switch' to control the flow of electricity to the bulb?
questions.n: The 'Hot' wire is always the one that is switched to ensure power is completely cut off from the fixture when the switch is open.

questions.q: What is the 'Maximum Demand' factor applied to the first 3000 VA of lighting load for a 'Hospital' according to the PEC?
questions.n: Like residential, the first 3000 VA of a hospital lighting load is calculated at 100% demand.

questions.q: Which type of lighting source is currently the most preferred in architectural design for its long life and low energy consumption?
questions.n: LEDs are the current industry standard due to their extreme energy efficiency and lifespan of 25,000+ hours.

questions.q: What happens if you use a '15-Ampere' circuit breaker for a circuit that has '12-gauge (3.5mm²)' wire?
o: The wire will melt because it is too thin for the breaker.
It will cause a short circuit automatically.
The circuit will not work at all.
It is a safe installation because the breaker will trip before the wire reaches its limit.
questions.n: The rule is that the breaker must protect the wire; since 12-gauge wire can handle 20A, a 15A breaker protects it perfectly.

questions.q: In an architectural reflected ceiling plan, what is the specific function of an 'S4' symbol?
o: A switch that controls four separate lighting circuits.
A four-way switch used in conjunction with two three-way switches.
To control a light from four different locations.
questions.n: The S4 or four-way switch is placed between two three-way switches to add additional control points in a circuit.

questions.q: What is the PEC-mandated minimum vertical clearance for service drop conductors passing over a public street or an alley subject to truck traffic?
questions.n: A minimum of 5.5 meters is required over public thoroughfares to ensure the tallest legal vehicles can pass safely.

questions.q: A residential 'Master Circuit Breaker' is sized primarily to protect which part of the electrical system?
o: The service entrance conductors and the entire panelboard.
The light bulbs in the ceiling fixtures.
The individual appliances plugged into outlets.
questions.n: The main breaker ensures that the total current drawn doesn't exceed the capacity of the main supply wires entering the building.

questions.q: When coordinating a project with a 'Generator,' what is the primary purpose of an 'Automatic Transfer Switch' (ATS)?
o: To increase the fuel efficiency of the generator engine.
To convert the generator's DC output into AC for the building.
To act as a secondary electric meter for the generator.
To sense a power failure and automatically switch the building load from the utility to the generator.
questions.n: The ATS provides a seamless transition to backup power without requiring manual intervention during an outage.

questions.q: In the Philippines, what is the standard diameter of the smallest 'Convenience Outlet' box used in residential masonry walls?
questions.n: The 2x4 inch rectangular box is the standard housing for single or duplex convenience outlets and switches.

questions.q: Which of the following is a requirement for 'Grounding Electrode' conductors (the wire going to the ground rod)?
o: It must be as long as possible to increase resistance.
It must be painted red to indicate danger.
It must be connected to the gas piping system.
It must be continuous, without any splices or joints.
questions.n: The PEC requires a continuous grounding path to ensure the connection never fails due to a loose splice during a surge.

questions.q: When calculating the number of 'General Purpose' branch circuits for a house, what is the maximum VA (Volt-Ampere) load usually assigned to a single 15-Ampere circuit?
questions.n: Applying the 80% rule for continuous use, a 15A circuit at 230V is often limited to roughly 1200-1300 VA for general planning.

questions.q: In a residential kitchen, why are 'Countertop' outlets required to be spaced so that no point along the wall is more than 600 mm from an outlet?
o: To increase the total electricity bill of the owner.
Because kitchen walls are usually weaker than living room walls.
To prevent the use of dangerous extension cords for kitchen appliances.
To make the kitchen look more modern.
questions.n: Kitchen appliances have short cords; frequent outlets ensure they can be plugged in directly without reaching across sinks or stoves.

questions.q: What is the minimum size of 'Copper' wire allowed for a standard 'Lighting' branch circuit in a residence?
questions.n: The PEC identifies 2.0 mm² (AWG No. 14 equivalent) as the minimum conductor size for residential lighting circuits.

questions.q: If an Architect sees 'TW' printed on an electrical wire, what does this designation indicate about the wire's insulation?
o: It is a 'Two-Way' wire for communication systems.
It is 'Twisted' and 'Wrapped' for extra strength.
questions.n: The 'T' stands for Thermoplastic and the 'W' indicates it is rated for wet or moisture-prone locations.

questions.q: Which of the following is the standard color for a 'Neutral' wire in a typical Philippine electrical system?
questions.n: The PEC designates white or light gray as the standard identifying color for grounded (neutral) conductors.

questions.q: What is the primary architectural purpose of a 'Service Entrance Cap' or Weatherhead?
o: To act as a mounting bracket for the electric meter.
To increase the voltage of the incoming power.
To hide the electrical wires for aesthetic reasons.
To prevent rain and moisture from entering the conduit system.
questions.n: The hooded design ensures that water cannot flow down the service mast and into the building's main panel.

questions.q: According to standard residential practice, at what height should a standard light switch be mounted from the finished floor line (FFL)?
questions.n: This range is the ergonomic standard for light switches, allowing comfortable reach for most adults.

questions.q: Which specific device is used to measure and record the amount of electrical energy consumed by a building for billing purposes?
questions.n: The meter measures the cumulative energy used in kilowatt-hours (kWh) over a period of time.

questions.q: A GFCI outlet is specifically required in which of the following areas of a house?
questions.n: Kitchens are 'wet areas' where the risk of electric shock is high due to proximity to sinks and liquids.

questions.q: What does a 'Single-Pole, Double-Throw' (SPDT) switch represent in common architectural electrical symbols?
questions.n: An S3 switch allows current to be 'thrown' to one of two paths, which is the definition of a Double-Throw switch.

questions.q: Which material is the standard for electrical conduits used in residential 'embedded' slab construction in the Philippines?
questions.n: PVC is the industry standard for slab embedding because it is corrosion-resistant, lightweight, and affordable.

questions.q: In a reflected ceiling plan, what does a circular symbol with four 'wings' or 'blades' typically represent?
questions.n: The four blades in the symbol are a literal representation of a ceiling fan's blades.

questions.q: Why is 'Grounding' essential in a residential electrical system?
o: To make the light bulbs shine brighter.
To provide a safe, low-resistance path for fault current to return to the earth.
To keep the electricity from leaking and increasing the bill.
To allow the electricity to travel faster through the wires.
questions.n: Grounding ensures that if a wire touches a metal casing, the electricity goes to the ground instead of through a person.

questions.n: The PEC designates white or light gray as the standard identifying color for grounded (neutral) conductors.

questions.q: What is the primary architectural purpose of a 'Service Entrance Cap' (Weatherhead)?
o: To prevent rain and moisture from entering the conduit system.
To act as a mounting bracket for the electric meter.
To hide electrical wires for aesthetic reasons.
To increase the voltage of the incoming power.
questions.n: The hooded design ensures that water cannot flow down the service mast and into the building's main panel.

questions.q: Which material is the most common choice for electrical conduits embedded within concrete floor slabs in the Philippines?
questions.n: PVC is the industry standard for slab embedding because it is corrosion-resistant, lightweight, and affordable.

questions.q: Which device is responsible for measuring and recording the cumulative electrical energy (kWh) consumed by a household?
questions.n: The meter measures the cumulative energy used over a period of time for billing purposes.

questions.q: What is the primary reason for providing 'Grounding' in an architectural electrical system?
o: To keep the electricity from leaking and increasing the bill.
To provide a safe, low-resistance path for fault current to return to the earth.
To allow electricity to travel faster through the wires.
To make light bulbs shine brighter.
questions.n: Grounding ensures that if a live wire touches a metal casing, the electricity is diverted safely away from people.

questions.q: A 'GFCI' outlet must be installed in which of the following areas according to safety standards?
questions.n: Kitchens are 'wet areas' where the risk of shock is high due to the proximity of sinks and appliances.

questions.q: What does a 'Single-Pole, Single-Throw' (SPST) switch represent in its simplest form?
questions.n: A standard S1 switch simply opens or closes one circuit at one point.
